thread:
sam: running the Python quickstart inside our CI job and the first API call is failing. It works locally. any ideas?

sam: job step: `docker run --rm -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=${REDWOOD_API_KEY} sample/python-quickstart`

sam: CI log snippet:
```
POST /v1/chat
Authorization: Bearer ***
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\ncontent-type: text/html\n\n<html>502 Bad Gateway</html>
```

sam: token is set via project secret; same secret used successfully from my laptop. CI yields 502, laptop yields 402 JSON `{\"error\":\"org_billing_required\"}`.
tess: is the CI runner on a corporate network or going through a runner-side proxy? 502 suggests a gateway, not auth.
sam: our runner is on a self-hosted k8s pool behind a sidecar. we also use short-lived workspace tokens minted by the web UI.

ops-bot: Reminder: CI token rotation policy: workspace tokens expire after 60m. Consider using a service key for non-interactive environments.
sam: i did try a service key and got a 403 inside CI. weirdly workspace token gave 502.

tess: that pattern matches header stripping by an ingress sidecar: when Authorization is removed, SDK retries and the upstream proxy returns HTML 502 instead of passing JSON 402. we've seen this with mod_security setups.

onboard-bot: Your org (velox-sandbox) does not have a billing method on file. New outbound requests may be blocked. Console: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/velox-sandbox/billing :credit_card:
sam: aha. dashboard quickstart didn't surface billing because web control plane uses a different check. CI surface is showing the upstream gateway 502 which hides the billing hint.
tess: workaround: use a service key mounted as a file and read it in the container (`-v ~/.redwood/service_key:/run/creds/service_key:ro` then `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat /run/creds/service_key)`) — some proxies preserve file-based env injection. also validate that your sidecar preserves Authorization header.
sam: confirmed: injecting service key file made the call return 402 with the `org_billing_required` body.
tess: action items: 1) devex doc about CI/runner proxies that remove Authorization and recommended secret mounting patterns, 2) CLI/SDK: preflight call to check org billing status and if missing, surface a clear error rather than letting gateway 502s obscure it, 3) ops: review runner sidecar config to pass through Authorization.
sam: opening an eng/devex ticket with CI job YAML, runner sidecar config, curl traces, and minimal repro. tagging @tess. thanks! :sparkles:
